narrative.text: The Lytheiran intermediary contacts you through the same secure channel through which the position was established. The short position against the Veltrian Krone has reached its settlement date. The 4,000 ₭ you placed in the leveraged foreign exchange position months ago has been riding on a single bet: that the Krone would fall. The intermediary's message is brief and clinical — the kind of message that would be innocuous to anyone who did not know what it meant, and devastating to anyone who did.

I bet against my own country's currency. Four thousand ₭, leveraged through foreign exchange markets, routed through a Lytheiran shell company, placed on the conviction that the Krone would decline. Every economic briefing I received, every policy decision I made, every statement I issued about the Veltrian economy — all of it was shadowed by the knowledge that I had a personal financial stake in the country's economic direction. If the economy crashed, I would profit. If I took steps to stabilize it, I would lose my investment. The question that will be asked — if anyone ever finds out — is whether I let the economy decline because it was unavoidable, or because it was profitable. The answer depends on what happens next.

choices.text: "The Krone has fallen. The position has paid out — 20,000 ₭, routed through the Lytheiran shell, deposited in the designated account. I told myself I was not betting against my country. I told myself I was hedging against uncertainty — protecting my family from the consequences of a crisis I was trying to prevent. But the crisis happened. Whether I could have prevented it — whether I tried hard enough to prevent it — is a question I will be asking myself for the rest of my life. The money is real. So is the cost of earning it. I will take the return. I will not pretend it feels like a victory."

"The Krone stabilized. The position has closed at a total loss — the 4,000 ₭ is gone. The leverage amplified the losses, and the Lytheiran intermediary confirms there is nothing to recover. I lost the bet. The country won. I should feel good about that — I put the country's interests ahead of my portfolio, I worked to stabilize the currency, I did not let my personal financial position influence my policy decisions. But I also made the bet in the first place. I was willing to profit from my country's economic decline. The fact that I lost the bet does not make me virtuous. It makes me lucky — lucky that my worst judgment did not pay off, and lucky that no one ever has to know about the position I took. Close the shell company. Destroy the records. This never happened."

"The position has closed — and I am disclosing it. Voluntarily. To the BCA, if one exists. To the press, if they will listen. I will tell them everything: the Lytheiran intermediary, the short position against the Krone, the 4,000 ₭ I invested and lost when the economy stabilized. I will tell them that I made a terrible judgment, that I bet against my own country, and that the only redeeming fact is that I lost the bet — because I worked to stabilize the currency, and my policy decisions were not influenced by my personal financial position. I will take whatever consequences follow. I earned them. But I will not spend the rest of my life waiting for someone to discover what I did. I would rather be judged than be afraid."
